sections.h2: Fastest way to sell in San Marcos
sections.html:
Selling for cash, with the house left as is, tends to wrap up first. No mortgage approval, no appraiser and no repair negotiation stand in the way. A listing might net more, though it demands prep work, showings and patience.

San Marcos is the Hays County seat, about 25 miles south of Austin on Interstate 35. Part of the city also falls in Guadalupe County, so check which appraisal district covers your lot before you read a tax statement.

Ask every buyer for a written offer, then set each one next to an agent's estimate of your take-home. The gap between the two is what speed costs you.

San Marcos leans toward renting. Owner occupancy runs 30.8 percent, the median value of an owned home is $310,400, and median gross rent is $1,322. The population estimate is 77,830, up 14.9 percent from the 2020 base.

Monthly owner costs average $1,899 with a mortgage and $706 without one. Because so many households rent, investors make up a big share of buyers for older or rougher houses. If your roof is tired or the foundation is a worry, those buyers may price the work more calmly than a first time owner would. The housing stock is mixed, from older homes near downtown to newer construction on the edges, so describe your house's age, systems and lot clearly when you talk to buyers.

Demand rises and falls with the school calendar and with hiring in Austin. Houses near campus appeal to a different crowd than houses near the highway, and buyers watch monthly cost closely. A home with working systems and few surprises is easier to move than one that looks cheap but needs work.

The city regulates rentals closely. Code Compliance requires owners of short term and long term rentals to register under city ordinances, and its officers cover more than 30 square miles. Before you commit to a closing date, verify that your rental registration is current. Code questions go to 512-393-8479.

San Marcos ISD is among the school districts listed by the Guadalupe Appraisal District, so it applies to parcels on that side of the county line. Hays County parcels use the Hays Central Appraisal District. Your bill shows which units tax you.

sections.h2: Checking or contesting your Hays County value
sections.html:
Start with the Hays Central Appraisal District's property search and interactive map. Its online forms cover homestead filings, agricultural use applications, business personal property renditions and change of address requests. Its office, at 21001 North IH 35 in Kyle, has a drop box by the front door.

Staff answer (512) 268-2522 and see visitors 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays. After August 7 of each year, Texas.gov/PropertyTaxes links to a local database showing the tax each unit would levy under its proposed rate, and owners can subscribe to alerts there.

The district also appraises through the year. Staff walk neighborhoods and commercial areas to measure new construction and update property details, so an addition you built without telling anyone can surface in your value. Make sure your records match the house a buyer will see.

sections.h2: Property taxes for a San Marcos seller
sections.html:
The Hays Central Appraisal District sets values and exemptions but sends no bills and takes no payments. Billing belongs to the Hays County Tax Office, which has no say over values. Texas collects no state property tax, so these dates apply to local units only.

Property tax timing for San Marcos owners
StepTiming
Value and lien dateJanuary 1
Homestead value noticesAbout April 1
Review board protestsBy mid May
Bills mailedOctober 1
Delinquent afterJanuary 31

The school portion of a homestead bill drops by $140,000 of value, and by $60,000 more if the owner is older or disabled. Hays CAD reviews each homestead every five years. When you leave, tell the district, and read the tax proration line on your closing paperwork.

Missing paperwork causes most delays. Find your deed and your latest tax bill, and look up your parcel on the district's search and interactive map to see what the district has on file. If you built an addition, check that the district has it right, because staff walk neighborhoods to measure new construction. If the house is a rental, have your city registration ready. A buyer or title company will ask about leases, so keep a copy of each one.

  • Deed or estate papers.
  • Latest tax bill and the county tax office payoff figure.
  • Rental registration, if the house is a rental.
  • Receipts for roof, plumbing and foundation work.

sections.h2: If you disagree with the appraised value
sections.html: Protests go to the review board, and the usual window runs to mid May. File through the district's online forms or bring your paperwork to the office in Kyle. Gather what you have on condition: repair estimates, photos and any receipts. A worn roof or a settling foundation is the kind of detail a board member can actually act on. A lower value also gives a buyer a lower starting tax estimate.

sections.h2: Pricing for the San Marcos buyer pool
sections.html: Think about who is likely to walk through your door. A household renting at $1,322 a month compares that figure with a mortgage payment, and the $1,899 average for owners with a loan is the number in their heads. An investor looks at the same house and sees rent potential near campus or along the Interstate 35 corridor. Describe the roof, foundation and systems plainly, and let buyers price the work themselves. Hays County and Guadalupe County parcels run on different appraisal districts, so confirm yours first and quote the right tax figure.

sections.h2: Your homestead exemption when you sell
sections.html: The exemption ends the day you move out. Where you had none, whoever buys after January 1 can claim one for what remains of the year. Let Hays CAD know you left, and ask the title company how the year's tax gets divided with the buyer.

Whichever county holds the land, its clerk records the deed. A notary or similar officer must witness the signature first. Recording runs $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for every page after it.

A house passed to an heir needs matching paperwork, such as an executor's deed, a will plus court order, or a death affidavit under a transfer on death deed. Your title company can tell you what a particular buyer will insist on.

sections.h2: Questions to ask before you sign
sections.html: Before any San Marcos contract goes out, run through a short list with the buyer. Who orders the title search, and who pays for it? Does the offer assume the roof and foundation stay as they are? What happens if the title company finds a lien or an unpaid tax balance? When is the money wired? A buyer who answers each point in writing is easier to trust than one who promises a fast close and leaves the details open. If the house has tenants or a rental registration, add them to the list so nothing surprises you on closing day.

Texas foreclosures are mostly nonjudicial and end in a public auction, so a private sale before that date can protect equity. To remove a tenant, the landlord needs written notice and a justice court order, though some buyers will take the lease as is.

Repairs are the easiest problem to hand off. An as is purchase moves the roof, plumbing and cosmetic work, and the contractor bids, to the buyer.

sections.h2: What a cash closing looks like
sections.html: After you accept, the title company starts a file and looks for liens, unpaid taxes and probate problems. Then you agree on a date and sign at its office. Bring photo ID, plus the deed or the estate papers. Any lien, tax balance or probate step can stretch the schedule, so ask the buyer to put the date in writing and decide who pays title and recording costs before signing.

faqs.q: Must I fix San Marcos repairs before selling?
faqs.a: No. An investor can buy the house in its current shape. You weigh that offer against a repaired listing.

faqs.q: Which office mails the tax bill for a San Marcos home?
faqs.a: It comes from the county tax office for the county that holds the parcel. For Hays County parcels that is the Hays County Tax Office, while the appraisal district only sets values and exemptions.

faqs.q: Does a San Marcos rental need registration?
faqs.a: Yes. Code Compliance requires short term and long term rental owners to register under city ordinances. Confirm yours before a closing.

faqs.q: How long will a cash sale take in San Marcos?
faqs.a: The timeline depends on title work and the buyer, so ask for a closing date on paper. Probate, liens or unpaid taxes can add time.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption move with me?
faqs.a: No. It ends at the move. If you had no exemption, whoever buys after January 1 may claim it for the rest of that year. Tell Hays CAD you left.
